record.paper_title: Some open questions in axion theory
record.original_question: What is the correct physical motivation and precise formulation of the axion Weak Gravity Conjecture, including the correct order-one coefficient c in the bound f_a S < c M_Pl, given that present cosmological constraints from the conjecture depend crucially on that coefficient and on a better understanding of gravitational instantons and Euclidean wormholes?

evidence.quote: Yet, the conjecture itself is quite mysterious: while the ordinary Weak Gravity Conjecture is motivated by demanding consistent black hole decay, the physical motivation underlying the axion Weak Gravity Conjecture is unclear, and the primary evidence for the conjecture comes simply from examples in string theory and from connections to the ordinary Weak Gravity Conjecture. The precise version of the axion Weak Gravity Conjecture is also an open question: the conjecture implies a bound faS < cMPl, where S is the instanton action and c is an order-one coefficient, but the precise value of the coefficient c is still debated.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider a four-dimensional effective theory of quantum gravity containing a compact pseudo-scalar (axion) field θ ≅ θ + 2π with decay constant f_a, i.e. with kinetic term (f_a^2/2)(∂θ)^2, coupled to Einstein gravity with reduced Planck mass M_Pl. Such a theory generically admits Euclidean instanton configurations (gravitational instantons / wormholes) carrying axionic charge, each contributing an action S to nonperturbative effects of the form e^{-S} cos(θ).

The axion Weak Gravity Conjecture (axion WGC) is the proposed statement that, in any such theory consistent with quantum gravity, there must exist an instanton with axionic charge whose action S obeys
    f_a · S ≤ c · M_Pl
for some universal order-one constant c > 0 independent of the theory.

Problem. Provide:
(a) A precise formulation of the axion WGC, specifying exactly which instantons are required to exist (lightest charged instanton; convex-hull-type condition over all charge directions in a multi-axion lattice; sub-lattice or tower form; inclusion or exclusion of gravitational instantons and Euclidean wormhole saddles).
(b) The exact value (or sharpest provable value) of the order-one coefficient c appearing in the bound f_a S ≤ c M_Pl, together with a derivation grounded in a physical principle analogous to the black-hole-decay motivation for the ordinary Weak Gravity Conjecture (for instance: consistency of the gravitational Euclidean path integral, absence of stable extremal/remnant configurations carrying axionic charge, or unitarity/positivity of axion scattering).
(c) A clear treatment of the role of gravitational instantons and Euclidean (Giddings–Strominger-type) wormholes in saturating or violating the bound, including whether such saddles count toward "the instanton" whose action enters the inequality.

A complete solution should reduce, in known controlled string-theoretic examples, to the bounds observed there, and should yield a definite cosmological implication for large-field axion inflation (where f_a ≳ M_Pl with S ≳ 1 is required).
artifact.status_search_result: The precise formulation of the axion Weak Gravity Conjecture and the exact value of the order-one coefficient c in the bound f_a S ≤ c M_Pl remain debated. Recent works (e.g. derivations from positivity of the gravitational path integral, and studies of axion strings) have proposed sharper versions, but no universally accepted formulation or value of c has emerged, and the role of gravitational instantons and Euclidean wormholes continues to be under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Positivity of the gravitational path integral implies the axionic weak gravity conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: A sharp version of the axion weak gravity conjecture, including precise numerical constants, derived from positivity constraints on gravitational path integrals.
status_evidence.claim: Recent attempts to derive a sharp form of the axion WGC indicate the precise coefficient remained unresolved prior to this work and is still being refined.

status_evidence.title: The Weak Gravity Conjecture: A Review (2201.08380)
status_evidence.snippet: Review discussing axion WGC variants, the role of gravitational instantons and wormholes, and the unresolved status of the order-one coefficient.
status_evidence.claim: The axion WGC has multiple inequivalent formulations and the order-one coefficient remains an open question.

status_evidence.title: The Weak Gravity Conjecture and Axion Strings (2108.11383)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses bound T ≤ c' f_a M_Pl on axion string tension with c' an undetermined O(1) coefficient.
status_evidence.claim: Order-one coefficients in axion-related WGC bounds remain to be pinned down.
